title: Make the .secrets.baseline route guard detect a present-but-inert invocation, not merely a present substring
rebase_note: Originally cut from 8d525dbe7fe94d755a26e631b9869e0b3bfbfc31, which is the base every measurement in premise_predictions_stated_before_measurement was taken against. main moved to 80c1684 (PR #68, Google Cloud provider) mid-slice and this branch was rebased onto it. progress.md was resolved by taking main's blob verbatim and re-appending; .secrets.baseline did not conflict because this slice never touched it, so #68's growth from 21 to 31 tracked files and 75 to 107 entries is preserved. Every gate and the twelve route cases were re-measured against the new base.
objective: tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py::test_every_route_invokes_the_validator asserts that four files still invoke the baseline validator, using a bare substring test: 'check_secrets_baseline' in text. A substring survives a comment character. The guard therefore constrains PRESENCE but not EFFECT, which is the same defect shape already found twice in this repository (a guard that asserted entries CHANGED without asserting HOW, and a fallback chain ending in a literal that always resolved). Replace the substring test with a check that extracts each file's EXECUTABLE content in that file's own language and asserts the invocation survives there, so a commented-out invocation is as red as a deleted one.
premise_predictions_stated_before_measur: P1 PREDICTED: on the untouched tree at 8d525db the route guard PASSES for all four files (positive control; a failure reported later means something only if this holds).
P2 PREDICTED: DELETING the invocation line makes the guard RED in all four of .github/workflows/ci.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/check.ps1, scripts/check.sh.

P3 PREDICTED: COMMENTING OUT the invocation line leaves the guard GREEN in all four, because a '#' prefix does not remove the substring. This is the defect. If measurement contradicts it, STOP and report rather than fixing what is not broken.

P4 PREDICTED: the four routes are three different languages (YAML, PowerShell, POSIX shell) plus shell nested inside YAML block scalars in ci.yml, so a single naive rule does not fit all four. ci.yml's invocation lives inside a 'run: |' block scalar, which is YAML data but shell CODE.

P5 PREDICTED: naive comment stripping (line.split('#')[0]) would corrupt real code in these files, because scripts/check.sh and ci.yml both contain ${#files[@]} / ${#FAILURES[@]} inside double quotes. Quote-aware scanning is therefore load-bearing, not decoration.
in_scope: tests/support/source_scan.py (new; stdlib-only executable-content extraction for YAML, PowerShell and POSIX shell)
tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py (replace the substring route guard; add in-memory mutation tests for delete and comment-out per route; add unit tests for the extractor itself)
out_of_scope_zero_diff: scripts/check_secrets_baseline.py and scripts/refresh_secrets_baseline.py. The validator is verified working end to end; this slice guards the WIRING, not the wiring itself. If the wiring proves defective, STOP and report instead of editing.
The exit-code branching in any of the four route files. The four route files must end byte-identical to base; they are the SUBJECT of the guard, not its target.

tests/fixtures/ingest/gcp/**, apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/profiles/gcp.py, config/examples/providers/gcp.example.yaml, docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md, scripts/url-allowlist.txt (a concurrent Google Cloud slice owns these)
agent-state/feature_list.json (byte-identical to base; no flag flipped; F008 stays passes:false)
apps/web/** (package-lock.json blob must stay f492053a91df9a977f6fda838ee82c6c38f5eda7), docker-compose.yml, apps/api/app/ingest/**, apps/api/app/classify/**
any manifest, lockfile, override or audit configuration. No new dependency: the extractor is standard library only, so the guard cannot be broken by an absent parser.
.secrets.baseline unless a tracked file's digests genuinely move, and then ONLY via python scripts/refresh_secrets_baseline.py
promotion or merge of the draft pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1 COMMENT-OUT IS RED: for each of the four route files, commenting out the invocation in that file's own comment syntax makes the guard fail.
A2 DELETION STAYS RED: for each of the four, deleting the invocation still makes the guard fail. The existing property must not be traded away for the new one.
A3 UNTOUCHED PASSES: each unmodified route file still passes. A false positive here teaches people to delete the guard, which is worse than the gap being closed.

A4 DESIGNED FROM THE PROPERTY, NOT THE INCIDENT: the check reasons about each file's actual comment syntax and executable regions, not a regex tuned to the one bypass in the brief. Quote-aware, here-doc/here-string aware, block-comment aware.

A5 LIMITS DECLARED: the present-but-inert modes considered are enumerated in the test module, split into caught and knowingly-not-caught. A guard whose limits are documented beats one whose limits are discovered later.

A6 PERMANENT, NOT ONE-OFF: delete and comment-out are asserted by tests operating on in-memory copies of the real files, so the property is re-measured on every run and needs no working-tree mutation.
A7 BYTE-EXACT RESTORE: any file mutated in the working tree for end-to-end measurement is restored byte-exactly, proved by git hash-object against git rev-parse ref:path, never numstat.
A8 NO CONTROL WEAKENED, NO TEST LOST: collected test count does not fall; no existing assertion is deleted or loosened.
A9 PROTECTED STATE: feature_list.json byte-identical, F008 still passes:false, zero diff to every locked path, the four route files byte-identical to base, progress.md insertions-only.
A10: the pull request is opened as a DRAFT and is not merged.
verification_plan: Re-derive origin/main with git ls-remote before branching and again immediately before reporting.
Bootstrap the venv FIRST; a fresh worktree lacks one and missing tooling produces phantom failures that prove nothing.
Positive control BEFORE anything else: the route guard passes on the untouched tree.
State the prediction for all twelve cases (4 files x delete/comment-out/untouched) BEFORE measuring, and record every place the prediction was wrong.
Measure the OLD guard's behaviour on all twelve cases to confirm the defect exists exactly as briefed, then the NEW guard's behaviour on the same twelve.
Drive the twelve cases through a script rather than by hand, so the measurement is deterministic and repeatable.
Never read an exit code through a truncating pipeline; Select-Object -First N corrupts $LASTEXITCODE. Capture the code immediately, and confirm any alarming result by a second method.
Quote git ranges as "$base..HEAD" so PowerShell does not split at the dot; run any filtered git diff UNFILTERED first as a positive control.
Read the PR's job-level CI status directly rather than trusting any inherited baseline claim.
Open a draft PR and inspect its state with gh pr view.
negative_tests: Comment-out must be RED in all four routes, in each file's own comment syntax (# for YAML, PowerShell and shell; additionally <# #> block comments for PowerShell).
Deletion must remain RED in all four routes.
A deleted route FILE must be red with a clear message rather than an unhandled traceback.
The extractor must not treat ${#files[@]} or ${#FAILURES[@]} as a comment; a naive stripper does, and that would be a false positive on correct code.
The extractor must not treat a '#' inside a quoted string as a comment.
An unconditional top-level early exit placed before the invocation must be RED for the shell-family routes.
data_implications: No migration, no schema change, no persisted state. Test-support code and tests only.
security_privacy: No network access, no credential material. The slice strengthens a guard that keeps a secret-scanning gate wired into all four routes; it does not touch the scanner or its exit-code handling.
portability: Standard library only; no new dependency and no YAML parser, so the guard cannot fail open or fail red because a parser is missing from an environment. Windows and POSIX both exercised: the extractor is pure text processing over bytes decoded as UTF-8.
z0_risk: Indirect but real. This guard is one of the mechanisms that keeps a secret-detection gate attached to every route into main. If it can be silenced by a '#', the gate can be silenced by a '#', and a leaked credential in a published evidence artefact is a far worse outcome than any classification error. No Z0 classification, quota calculation, or provider evidence is touched by this slice.
